name: January 25, 2023 - Regular Meeting
agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID19
and pursuant to the AB361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
September 22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote,
and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting .

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bayala@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as
states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal
emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person
would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the
Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests
that you sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Mayor and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the Public Works Department, and available upon request by emailing bayala@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 19th day of January 2023, at 4:00 p.m.

  ______________________________________
  Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  speeding concerns on Big Rock Drive and look into painting the speed limit onto

  In response to Chair Major, Public Works Director DuBoux stated staff would

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Director DuBoux updated the Commission Planning Department was
  preparing a memo to be presented to City Council discussing the tower that was
  installed at the Santa Monica College site. Additionally, the Outdoor Warning
  Sirens project will be presented to Public Safety and Public Works Commissions at
  a future joint meeting. Caltrans was granted an extension to work in the creek
  through December from Department of Fish and Game for the Trancas Bridge
  Replacement Project. Lastly, Public Works Director DuBoux reported revised
  flood maps were very close to FEMA approving the revised flood maps.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart provided an update on the City’s maintenance
  crews clean up to the recent storms.

  Assistant Public Works Director Spayd announced the seawall near Big Rock Drive
  would be heard by the Planning Commission on November 21, 2022 and his
  departure from the City would be December 2.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  In response to Vice Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  Caltrans’ ability to install the necessary bridge piles at their new depth.

  In response to Commissioner Drummond, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  that the Commission could request telecommunications to be added to the work
  plan at an upcoming Public Works Commission meeting.

  Vice Chair Dittrich reported he met with Planning Director Mollica to discuss
  details of the approved details of the Santa Monica College site and installed
  antenna.

  In response to Chair Major, Public Works Director DuBoux stated staff had been
  in continuous communication with the construction team for the Trancas Bridge
  Replacement Project and staff was aware of the field issues.

  Vice Chair Dittrich discussed his concerns about a potential mural near Malibu
  Seafood.

  Aladjadjian discussed her concern about Mountains Recreation Conservation
  Authority (MRCA) not performing their landscape maintenance at the Vista Point

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) Malibu Lower-Cost
  Accommodations Public Works Plan
  Staff recommendation: Provide a recommendation to the City Council regarding
  the City’s representative comments to the MRCA Lower-Cost Accommodations
  Public Works Plan.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the staff report.

  Terry Davis discussed her concern about the proposed project. She further stated
  there was concern with MRCA inability to maintain their existing sites. She would
  like the City to unite and provide responses to Joe Edmiston’s superiors.
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Special Meeting

Page 4 of 8

  E. Barry Haldeman questioned who had jurisdiction over property next to Malibu
  Bluffs Park and property at Ramirez Canyon. He discussed his concerns about the
  coordination between Los Angeles County Fire Department, Los Angeles County
  Sheriff’s Department and the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors. He
  suggested the City form a Citizen’s Commission to work with Public Works
  Commission to address the proposed project.

  Ryan Embree suggested the City reject the proposed project. He stated there was a
  similar case with the Ramirez Canyon Preservation fund and MRCA that included
  camp sites. He discussed the 2007 fire that burnt homes on Malibu Road and part
  of Malibu Bluffs Park. He stated there was a settlement agreement between the
  City and MRCA that included payment to the City in the amount of $200,000.

  Bill Sampson expressed his concerns about the MRCA proposed project.

  Chair Wade discussed CEQA concerns brought up by Craig Hill during the recent
  public scoping meeting held by MRCA. He stated the project as proposed should
  be classified as development and not improvements. He suggested the existing
  campgrounds and other properties held my MRCA be audited on capacity usage
  and see if those sites are under used. He questioned the proposed medical building
  when UCLA and Malibu Urgent Care already available in the City. He stated the
  project was in ESHA and there are proposed restrooms as part of the project. He
  questioned how MRCA will staff the proposed camp sites with resources already
  limited in the area. He questioned the need to construct an amphitheater and traffic
  impact to the neighboring community. He expressed his concerns about the noise
  impact and compliance with the City’s Dark Sky ordinance and the need for
  required studies. He suggested that MRCA not move forward with the project as
  an alternative to the proposed project. He stated there would need to be more
  justification on the proposed location in Ramirez Canyon.

  Commissioner Simmens stated there was a new opportunity with the newly elected
  City Council and new supervisor to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors.
  He suggested brief the new City Council and Los Angeles County Board of
  Supervisors.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated that staff had a specific timeline to respond
  to MRCA’s proposed project and provide all the comments and concerns.

  Commissioner Drummond stated the proposed project was a development and
  should adhere to the City’s Local Coastal Plan. She expressed her concern about
  proposed project to include restrooms when it is located in an ESHA.

Special Meeting
Minutes of November 10, 2022
Page 5 of 8

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the part of the project proposed at Malibu
  Bluffs Park is located in the septic prohibition zone and would not be allowed. He
  further explained staff would include all comments including traffic impacts.

  Commissioner Merrick questioned whether the Ramirez location within the City
  limits and may need to investigate the City’s ridgeline ordinance. He stated there
  was a fire at Malibu Bluffs Park in 2007 that burnt right to Malibu Road and has
  concerns about the proposed project. He stated he did not support the camping
  element but would be fine with the park elements. He stated there was history in
  the past that these types of projects had no oversight and they were completed.

  Vice Chair Dittrich stated the proposed project was not needed for the Malibu
  community. He expressed his concern about the impact of the proposed
  development and the need to keep Malibu rural. He stated the proposed project was
  in direct violation of Joe Edmiston’s mandate of developing in the Santa Monica
  mountains. He stated that City Council should reject the proposed project. He also
  expressed concern about impact to the view corridor.

  Vice Chair Dittrich moved and Chair Major seconded a motion the Public Works
  Commission reject the proposed project and recommended the City Council reject
  the proposed project and the City do every measure necessary to fight both of the
  proposed projects.

  Commissioner Drummond stated there are geological issues at the proposed
  locations.

  Vice Chair Dittrich stated the proposed locations should only be a day-use.

  Commissioner Merrick suggested the motion be voted on and additional motions
  afterwards.

  Public Works Director DuBoux reviewed and listed comments and concerns with
  the Commission and public comments 1) an audit for the need of campgrounds in
  the area 2) concern about the staffing levels for both proposed locations and the
  lack there of 3) question the need of a medical facility when facilities are available
  nearby 4) issues with the septic systems proposed at Malibu Bluffs Park because it
  is located in the prohibition zone and Ramirez Canyon located in ESHA 5) concerns
  about constructing an amphitheater would increase density, congestion, fire
  concerns, and traffic issues 6) concerns about noise, lighting 7) concerns about the
  necessity of the proposed development and meeting the City’s dark sky
  requirements 8) the proposed and existing trails are not suitable for night use
  especially during a campground 9) the alternative for the project would be not to
  do it 10) there are concerns about traffic issues at both proposed locations including
  driveway entrances and increased congestion in the neighborhoods 11) at the
  Ramirez Canyon location, it is located in extreme fire danger zone where several
 Malibu Public Works Commission

  homes have burned on small fires 12) there is an issue on development being
  proposed on a ridgeline 13) the proposed location in the Malibu Bluffs area is also
  located in an extreme fire danger zone where past fires have expanded and
  substantial damage to the community below 14) if a development does move
  forward, no camping should be included 15) concerns that at both proposed
  locations there would be impacts to the view preservation within the area 16) both
  sites have geological challenges for development.

  Commissioner Drummond stated there were documents from the Malibu Open
  Space Alliance discussing concerns about the blue-line streams and steep slopes
  used in previous proposed development in these areas.

  In response to Commissioner Merrick, Public Works Director DuBoux stated he
  believed the designation would need to be a natural preserve similar to natural
  preserve in point dume to prevent development on these locations.

  In response to Commissioner Drummond, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  that the suggestion would include day-use only.

  Vice Chair Dittrich withdrew his motion.

MOTION  Vice Chair Dittrich moved and Chair Major seconded a motion to strongly reject
  the development proposal of the MRCA Malibu Lower Cost Accommodations
  Public Works Plan. Preserve and designate Ramirez Canyon and Bluffs Park as
  open space and include many concerns conveyed by the community participants
  and the Public Works Commissioners at the November 10, 2022 Special Meeting
  1) audit for the actual need of campgrounds in the area; 2) concern about lack of
  staff levels for both campgrounds; 3) the need and necessity of having a medical
  building when there is ample facilities nearby; 4) need to install septic is within the
  prohibition zone Phase III as part of the MOU with the State; 5) proposed Ramirez
  Canyon site is located in ESHA and cannot install septic; 6) concerns about the
  amphitheater with increased density and congestion and fire concerns and noise
  pollution and lighting; 7) concerns about the lighting not meeting the City’s Dark
  Sky Ordinance; 8) proposed trails and existing trails are not suitable or sate for
  night-use; 9) substantial concerns related to traffic issues with both sites; 10)
  Ramirez Canyon site is in an extreme fire danger zone where there have been past
  wildfires; 11) Bluffs Park site is also located in an extreme fire danger zone where
  fires have been present in the past and had significant damage to the homes below;
  12) there should be no camping; 13) there is an excess strain on emergency services
  already within the area; 14) each site should only be used for day-use; 15)
  development at both sites will impact the view preservation within those areas; 16)
  wildlife specific to the Santa Monica Mountains; 17) burden to evacuate and
  administer shelter in-place for earthquakes and tsunamis, etc. The question was
  called, and the motion passed unanimously.

  B.  Mid-Year Report to the City Council
  Staff recommendation: Develop a list of Commission’s activities for the period of
  July through December 2022 to be included in the City Manager’s Mid-Year

  Assistant Public Works Director Spayd presented the staff report and discussed the

  In response to Assistant Public Works Director Spayd, Senior Administrative

  In response to Chair Wade, Assistant Public Works Director Spayd stated a future
  item about the operation and maintenance of landslide districts would come before

  By consensus, the Commission approved the list of Commission’s activities for the period

  meeting on January 23, 2023.

  C.  Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects Status Report
  Staff recommendation: Receive and file report on the status of the City’s current
  and upcoming Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

  Assistant Public Works Director Spayd presented the Commission with an update
  on the City’s Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

  In response to Chair Wade, Assistant Public Works Director Spayd stated the Public
  Works department provided constructability comments on the Permanent Skate
  Park. Public Works Director DuBoux further explained it was typical Public Works

  Public Works Superintendent Hart provided an update on the construction status of
  the Broad Beach Road Biofiltration Repair project, Bluffs Shade Structure project,
  Michael Landon HVAC Unit Repair project and the Point Dume Decomposed
  Granite Walkway Repair Project.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the Public Works Department will be

MOTION  At 5:48 p.m., Chair Major adjourned the meeting.

Subject:  Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update on the Five-Year Capital Improvement
Plan for Fiscal Years 2023-2028.

DISCUSSION: The City of Malibu’s public infrastructure is essential to providing safe and
reliable services for the community and visitors. The 2023-2028 Capital Improvement
Plan (CIP) provides a framework for identifying, planning, budgeting, prioritizing, and
implementing capital improvement projects within the city. In fiscal years 2022-2027, the
City anticipates spending approximately $187.9 million and working on 63 projects. In
fiscal year 2022-2023, the City anticipates spending approximately $35 million and
working on 28 capital projects. These projects will improve the public infrastructure,
improve safety and preserve the City’s largest assets. The CIP also identifies several
improvement and repair projects that were generated from the Woolsey Fire and
subsequent storm events.

Last year, staff has prepared a Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan spanning over fiscal
years 2022-2027 and was approved by City Council on August 22, 2022. The current plan
needs to be updated to include the projects anticipated for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 and to
add new projects to the plan. The Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan for Fiscal Years
2023-2028 will be coordinated with the City’s budget and will be sent to City Council in
July or August for final approval.

To:  Chair Major and Members of the Public Works Commission

Prepared by:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director/City Engineer

Date prepared:  December 28, 2022  Meeting date: January 25, 2023

Subject:  Neighborhood Beautification Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION:  Receive a presentation  regarding  Neighborhood
Beautification Programs and provide comments.

DISCUSSION:  At the November 10, 2022 Public Works Commission meeting,
Commissioner Drummond commented on a potential program that would allow the
community to participate in beautification projects within their neighborhood. Other cities
have similar neighborhood beautification programs, and that the City should investigate
these types of programs. These programs allow the public to install various improvements
within the public right of way that beautify their neighborhood.

Neighborhood beautification programs are designed to create a mechanism for the
community to create beautification improvements within the public right of way. They
create a way to clean and beautify Malibu by forming partnerships with volunteers,
residents, community organizations focusing on beautification efforts.

Staff has conducted research on various cities that implement neighborhood beautification
programs. Most of the programs allow the public, community members and homeowners
association to perform the improvements, contain the types of projects allowed under the
program, include improvement standards, and include procedures to submit the proposed
improvements.

Neighborhood beautification programs contain specific standards for the type and
specifics of the various improvements. These standards provide a guidance to the
community on what types of improvements can be done, the types of materials that can
be used and provides a consistency with the neighborhood characteristics. Providing
standards also ensures that the improvements do not create an unsafe condition and do
not cause any additional unreasonable maintenance efforts.

Here is a list of types of projects other agencies have included in their programs:

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 4.A.
   •  Murals or other public art
  •  Installation of landscaping including plants and trees
  •  Removal of weeds and other non-native landscaping
  •  New neighborhood entryway signs
  •  Removal and/or replacement of chain link fences
  •  New walkways
  •  Neighborhood cleanup events

Most of the programs require an application to be submitted to the Public Works
Department for review and approval. Some agencies require the applicant to be a
community-based organization, such as a homeowner’s association, neighborhood
groups, Chambers of Commerce and student groups. Other agencies send the
applications to City Council for final approval. Proposed projects should have the support
within their neighborhood. Petitions or other documents should be submitted to ensure
the community’s acceptance of the proposed project.

Maintenance of the improvements was also addressed in the programs. Improvements
within the right of way are typically the responsibility of the City to maintain. However,
some neighborhood beautification programs make the applicant or neighborhood
responsible for the maintenance. Any failure to adequately maintain the improvements
could result in removal by the public agency.

Some programs have the ability to issue grant funding associated with a neighborhood
beautification project. The grants are typically administered by a city committee who
reviews the applications and awards the grants based upon the program’s criteria and
objectives. Projects should have a minimum budget and should have a timeline on which
they will intend to use the funds.

Staff is seeking comments on whether the Public Works Commission would like to
recommend this type of program to City Council.
